questions.prompt: Which of the following is a common technique to ensure a model stays performant after deployment?

options.text: Retraining only at the end of the year

questions.explanation: Continuous monitoring allows early detection of performance degradation caused by data drift or concept drift.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of using a feature store in a production ML pipeline?

options.text: Reduces the number of training epochs
Ensures consistency between training and serving features

questions.explanation: A feature store centralizes feature definitions so the same transformations are applied during training and inference, preventing feature drift.

questions.prompt: Which strategy is most effective for rolling out a new model version with minimal risk?
questions.explanation: Canary releases expose the new model to a small subset of traffic, allowing quick rollback if issues arise.

questions.prompt: In a model monitoring dashboard, which metric would best indicate that the input data distribution has shifted?
questions.explanation: Divergence metrics compare current feature distributions to the training distribution, flagging distribution shifts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following practices helps ensure compliance with data privacy regulations in ML model deployment?

options.text: Storing raw user data in the model weights
Using differential privacy during training and limiting data retention

questions.explanation: Differential privacy protects individual data points, and limiting retention reduces exposure risks, aligning with privacy laws.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of model versioning in a CI/CD pipeline for ML?

options.text: To track changes and enable rollback

questions.explanation: Versioning records model artifacts, facilitating reproducibility and rollback when newer versions underperform.
